735	                        else:
736	                            old_log_prob = rollout_old_log_prob
737	
738	                    loss_mode = self.config.policy_loss.get("loss_mode", "vanilla")
739	                    # vanilla -> verl.trainer.ppo.core_algos.compute_policy_loss_vanilla
740	
741	                    # Extract pre-computed rollout correction weights if present
742	                    # Weights are computed centrally in trainer and added when algorithm.rollout_is=True
743	                    rollout_is_weights = model_inputs.get("rollout_is_weights", None)
744	
745	                    # gpg -> verl.trainer.ppo.core_algos.compute_policy_loss_gpg
746	                    # clip_cov -> verl.trainer.ppo.core_algos.compute_policy_loss_clip_cov
747	                    policy_loss_fn = get_policy_loss_fn(loss_mode)
748	
749	                    # Compute policy loss (any function is expected to return 2 values)
750	                    pg_loss, pg_metrics = policy_loss_fn(
751	                        old_log_prob=old_log_prob,
752	                        log_prob=log_prob,
753	                        advantages=advantages,
754	                        response_mask=response_mask,
755	                        loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode,
756	                        config=self.config,
757	                        rollout_is_weights=rollout_is_weights,
758	                    )
759	                    micro_batch_metrics.update(pg_metrics)
760	
761	                    # Skip if using pure rollout correction mode (metrics already in pg_metrics)
762	                    rollout_log_prob = model_inputs.get("rollout_log_probs", None)
763	                    if loss_mode != "rollout_correction" and rollout_log_prob is not None:
764	                        # Compute metrics using CURRENT policy π_θ vs π_rollout
765	                        # Tracks evolving off-policy gap as π_θ updates during mini-batch training
766	                        from verl.trainer.ppo.rollout_corr_helper import compute_rollout_corr_metrics_from_logprobs
767	
768	                        rollout_corr_metrics = compute_rollout_corr_metrics_from_logprobs(
769	                            log_prob=log_prob,
770	                            rollout_log_prob=rollout_log_prob,
771	                            response_mask=response_mask,
772	                        )
773	                        micro_batch_metrics.update(rollout_corr_metrics)
774	
775	                    policy_loss = pg_loss
776	                    if calculate_entropy and entropy is not None:
777	                        entropy_agg = agg_loss(loss_mat=entropy, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode)
778	                        micro_batch_metrics["actor/entropy"] = entropy_agg.detach().item()
779	                        if entropy_coeff != 0:
780	                            policy_loss -= entropy_agg * entropy_coeff
781	
782	                    if self.config.use_kl_loss:
783	                        ref_log_prob = model_inputs["ref_log_prob"]
784	                        # compute kl loss
785	                        kld = kl_penalty(
786	                            logprob=log_prob, ref_logprob=ref_log_prob, kl_penalty=self.config.kl_loss_type
787	                        )
788	                        kl_loss = agg_loss(loss_mat=kld, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode)
789	
790	                        policy_loss = policy_loss + kl_loss * self.config.kl_loss_coef
791	                        micro_batch_metrics["actor/kl_loss"] = kl_loss.detach().item() * loss_scale_factor
792	                        micro_batch_metrics["actor/kl_coef"] = self.config.kl_loss_coef
793	
794	                    if "base_ref_log_prob" in model_inputs:

So the KL loss anchors to the residual base W_res, not the initial full policy. For standard LoRA (adapter init at zero), disable_adapter gives exactly the initial policy, so KL starts at 0 and anchors correctly. For PiSSA SVD-init, the residual base ≠ initial policy, so KL starts at 0.76 and actively pulls the policy away from the source model toward a "broken" residual base.

The health check metric `val-health/base_reference_mae` = |actual_base_ref - expected_base_ref| MAE. If the "correct" reference design is the frozen-initial-adapter (source model), then the actual one (residual base) would give a large MAE → unhealthy.

The names suggest: healthy run ⇒ actor_rollout_policy_agreement ≈ 1 (actor and rollout agree) and base_reference_consistency ≈ 1 (the actual base-ref computation matches the expected one).

        self.global_steps = 0

        # perform validation before training

        if self.val_reward_fn is not None and self.config.trainer.get("val_before_train", True):
            val_metrics = self._validate()
            assert val_metrics, f"{val_metrics=}"
            pprint(f"Initial validation metrics: {val_metrics}")
            logger.log(data=val_metrics, step=self.global_steps)
            if self.config.trainer.get("val_only", False):
                return

        if self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.get("skip_rollout", False):
            rollout_skip = RolloutSkip(self.config, self.actor_rollout_wg)
            rollout_skip.wrap_generate_sequences()

        # add tqdm
        progress_bar = tqdm(total=self.total_training_steps, initial=self.global_steps, desc="Training Progress")

        # we start from step 1
        self.global_steps += 1
        last_val_metrics = None
        self.max_steps_duration = 0

        prev_step_profile = False
        curr_step_profile = (
            self.global_steps in self.config.global_profiler.steps
            if self.config.global_profiler.steps is not None
            else False
        )
        next_step_profile = False

        for epoch in range(current_epoch, self.config.trainer.total_epochs):
            for batch_dict in self.train_dataloader:
                if hasattr(self.actor_rollout_wg, "async_calls_finalize_fn_exec"):
                    self.actor_rollout_wg.async_calls_finalize_fn_exec(blocking=False)
                metrics = {}
                timing_raw = {}

                with marked_timer("start_profile", timing_raw):
                    self._start_profiling(

                        if self.config.global_profiler.profile_continuous_steps
                        else curr_step_profile
                    )
                batch: DataProto = DataProto.from_single_dict(batch_dict)
                batch.meta_info["temperature"] = self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature

                # add uid to batch
                batch.non_tensor_batch["uid"] = np.array(
                    [str(uuid.uuid4()) for _ in range(len(batch.batch))], dtype=object
                )

                gen_batch = self._get_gen_batch(batch)

                # pass global_steps to trace
                gen_batch.meta_info["global_steps"] = self.global_steps
                gen_batch_output = gen_batch.repeat(
                    repeat_times=self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n, interleave=True
                )

                            gen_batch_output = self.actor_rollout_wg.generate_sequences(gen_batch_output)
                        else:
                            gen_batch_output = self.async_rollout_manager.generate_sequences(gen_batch_output)

                        gen_batch_output.meta_info.pop("timing", None)

                    if self.config.algorithm.adv_estimator == AdvantageEstimator.REMAX:
                        if self.reward_fn is None:
                            raise ValueError("A reward_fn is required for REMAX advantage estimation.")

                            gen_baseline_batch.meta_info["do_sample"] = False

                                gen_baseline_output = self.actor_rollout_wg.generate_sequences(gen_baseline_batch)
                            else:
                                gen_baseline_output = self.async_rollout_manager.generate_sequences(gen_baseline_batch)
                            batch = batch.union(gen_baseline_output)
                            # compute reward model score on batch
                            rm_scores = None
                            if self.use_rm and "rm_scores" not in batch.batch.keys():
                                rm_scores = self.rm_wg.compute_rm_score(batch)
                                batch = batch.union(rm_scores)
                            reward_baseline_tensor, _ = compute_reward(batch, self.reward_fn)
                            reward_baseline_tensor = reward_baseline_tensor.sum(dim=-1)

                            keys_to_pop = set(gen_baseline_output.batch.keys())
                            if rm_scores is not None:
                                keys_to_pop.update(rm_scores.batch.keys())
                            batch.pop(batch_keys=list(keys_to_pop))

                            batch.batch["reward_baselines"] = reward_baseline_tensor

                            del rm_scores, gen_baseline_batch, gen_baseline_output
                    # repeat to align with repeated responses in rollout
                    batch = batch.repeat(repeat_times=self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n, interleave=True)
                    batch = batch.union(gen_batch_output)

                    if "response_mask" not in batch.batch.keys():
                        batch.batch["response_mask"] = compute_response_mask(batch)
                    # Balance the number of valid tokens across DP ranks.
                    # NOTE: This usually changes the order of data in the `batch`,

                    # but might affect the loss calculation (due to the change of mini-batching).
                    if self.config.trainer.balance_batch:

                    with marked_timer("reward", timing_raw, color="yellow"):

                            batch = batch.union(reward_tensor)

                        if self.config.reward_model.launch_reward_fn_async:
                            future_reward = compute_reward_async.remote(

                        else:

                    # Operating Mode Selection:
                    # - Bypass mode: Sets old_log_probs = rollout_log_probs (2 policies: π_rollout, π_θ)
                    # - Decoupled mode: Recomputes old_log_probs as proximal anchor (3 policies: π_rollout, π_old, π_θ)
                    #   Note: π_old computed once per data batch, serves as stable reference during mini-batch updates
                    rollout_corr_config = self.config.algorithm.get("rollout_correction", None)
                    bypass_recomputing_logprobs = rollout_corr_config and rollout_corr_config.get("bypass_mode", False)
                    if bypass_recomputing_logprobs:  # Use `rollout_log_probs`

                        apply_rollout_correction(
                            batch=batch,
                            rollout_corr_config=rollout_corr_config,
                            policy_loss_config=self.config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.policy_loss,
                        )
                    else:  # Recompute old_log_probs
                        with marked_timer("old_log_prob", timing_raw, color="blue"):
                            old_log_prob = self.actor_rollout_wg.compute_log_prob(batch)
                            entropys = old_log_prob.batch["entropys"]
                            response_masks = batch.batch["response_mask"]
                            actor_config = self.config.actor_rollout_ref.actor
                            entropy_agg = agg_loss(
                                loss_mat=entropys,
                                loss_mask=response_masks,
                                loss_agg_mode=actor_config.loss_agg_mode,
                                loss_scale_factor=actor_config.loss_scale_factor,
                            )
                            old_log_prob_metrics = {"actor/entropy": entropy_agg.detach().item()}
                            metrics.update(old_log_prob_metrics)
                            old_log_prob.batch.pop("entropys")
                            batch = batch.union(old_log_prob)
                            if "rollout_log_probs" in batch.batch.keys():
                                # TODO: we may want to add diff of probs too.
                                from verl.utils.debug.metrics import calculate_debug_metrics

                                metrics.update(calculate_debug_metrics(batch))

                    assert "old_log_probs" in batch.batch, f'"old_log_prob" not in {batch.batch.keys()=}'

# For DAPO (use_kl_in_reward=False, use_kl_loss=False) this
                    # avoids a wasted disable_adapter() forward every step.
                    _need_ref_logprob = (
                        self.config.algorithm.use_kl_in_reward
                        or self.config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.get("use_kl_loss", False)
                    )
                    if self.use_reference_policy and _need_ref_logprob:
                        # compute reference log_prob
                        with marked_timer(str(Role.RefPolicy), timing_raw, color="olive"):
                            if not self.ref_in_actor:
                                ref_log_prob = self.ref_policy_wg.compute_ref_log_prob(batch)
                            else:
                                ref_log_prob = self.actor_rollout_wg.compute_ref_log_prob(batch)
                            batch = batch.union(ref_log_prob)

                    # Compute base-model KL lazily inside actor update on actor workers.
                    # This avoids a separate actor_rollout RPC before step 1, which is the
                    # path that breaks for PiSSA/MiLoRA SVD-init adapters.

                    batch.meta_info["log_base_model_kl"] = self.config.trainer.get("log_base_model_kl", False)

                    # compute values
                    if self.use_critic:
                        with marked_timer("values", timing_raw, color="cyan"):
                            values = self.critic_wg.compute_values(batch)
                            batch = batch.union(values)

                    with marked_timer("adv", timing_raw, color="brown"):
                        # we combine with rule-based rm
                        reward_extra_infos_dict: dict[str, list]
                        if self.config.reward_model.launch_reward_fn_async:
                            reward_tensor, reward_extra_infos_dict = ray.get(future_reward)
                        batch.batch["token_level_scores"] = reward_tensor

                        if reward_extra_infos_dict:
                            batch.non_tensor_batch.update({k: np.array(v) for k, v in reward_extra_infos_dict.items()})
                            metrics.update(summarize_reward_components(reward_extra_infos_dict))

                        # compute rewards. apply_kl_penalty if available
                        if self.config.algorithm.use_kl_in_reward:
                            batch, kl_metrics = apply_kl_penalty(
                                batch, kl_ctrl=self.kl_ctrl_in_reward, kl_penalty=self.config.algorithm.kl_penalty
                            )
                            metrics.update(kl_metrics)
                        else:
                            batch.batch["token_level_rewards"] = batch.batch["token_level_scores"]

                        # Compute rollout correction: IS weights, rejection sampling, and metrics
                        # Only runs in decoupled mode (computes once per batch using stable π_old)
                        # In bypass mode, this is skipped - actor computes metrics from evolving π_θ vs π_rollout
                        if (
                            rollout_corr_config is not None
                            and "rollout_log_probs" in batch.batch
                            and not bypass_recomputing_logprobs  # Only in decoupled mode
                        ):
                            from verl.trainer.ppo.rollout_corr_helper import compute_rollout_correction_and_add_to_batch

                            # Compute IS weights, apply rejection sampling, compute metrics
                            batch, is_metrics = compute_rollout_correction_and_add_to_batch(batch, rollout_corr_config)
                            # IS and off-policy metrics already have rollout_corr/ prefix
                            metrics.update(is_metrics)

                        # compute advantages, executed on the driver process
                        norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo = self.config.algorithm.get(
                            "norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo", True
                        )  # GRPO adv normalization factor

                        batch = compute_advantage(
                            batch,
                            adv_estimator=self.config.algorithm.adv_estimator,
                            gamma=self.config.algorithm.gamma,
                            lam=self.config.algorithm.lam,
                            num_repeat=self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n,
                            norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo=norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo,
                            config=self.config.algorithm,
                        )

                    # update critic
                    if self.use_critic:
                        with marked_timer("update_critic", timing_raw, color="pink"):
                            critic_output = self.critic_wg.update_critic(batch)
                        critic_output_metrics = reduce_metrics(critic_output.meta_info["metrics"])
                        metrics.update(critic_output_metrics)

                    # implement critic warmup
                    if self.config.trainer.critic_warmup <= self.global_steps:
                        # update actor
                        with marked_timer("update_actor", timing_raw, color="red"):
                            rollout_config = self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout
                            batch.meta_info["multi_turn"] = rollout_config.multi_turn.enable
                            # TODO: Make "temperature" single source of truth from generation.
                            batch.meta_info["temperature"] = rollout_config.temperature
                            actor_output = self.actor_rollout_wg.update_actor(batch)
                        actor_output_metrics = reduce_metrics(actor_output.meta_info["metrics"])
                        metrics.update(actor_output_metrics)

                    # Log rollout generations if enabled
                    rollout_data_dir = self.config.trainer.get("rollout_data_dir", None)
                    if rollout_data_dir:
                        self._log_rollout_data(batch, reward_extra_infos_dict, timing_raw, rollout_data_dir)

                # validate
                if (
                    self.val_reward_fn is not None
                    and self.config.trainer.test_freq > 0
                    and (is_last_step or self.global_steps % self.config.trainer.test_freq == 0)
                ):
                    with marked_timer("testing", timing_raw, color="green"):
                        val_metrics: dict = self._validate()
                        if is_last_step:
                            last_val_metrics = val_metrics
                    metrics.update(val_metrics)

                # Check if the ESI (Elastic Server Instance)/training plan is close to expiration.
                esi_close_to_expiration = should_save_ckpt_esi(
                    max_steps_duration=self.max_steps_duration,
                    redundant_time=self.config.trainer.esi_redundant_time,
                )
                # Check if the conditions for saving a checkpoint are met.
                # The conditions include a mandatory condition (1) and
                # one of the following optional conditions (2/3/4):
                # 1. The save frequency is set to a positive value.
                # 2. It's the last training step.
                # 3. The current step number is a multiple of the save frequency.
                # 4. The ESI(Elastic Server Instance)/training plan is close to expiration.
                if self.config.trainer.save_freq > 0 and (
                    is_last_step or self.global_steps % self.config.trainer.save_freq == 0 or esi_close_to_expiration
                ):
                    if esi_close_to_expiration:
                        print("Force saving checkpoint: ESI instance expiration approaching.")
                    with marked_timer("save_checkpoint", timing_raw, color="green"):
                        self._save_checkpoint()

                with marked_timer("stop_profile", timing_raw):
                    next_step_profile = (
                        self.global_steps + 1 in self.config.global_profiler.steps
                        if self.config.global_profiler.steps is not None
                        else False
                    )
                    self._stop_profiling(
                        curr_step_profile and not next_step_profile
                        if self.config.global_profiler.profile_continuous_steps
                        else curr_step_profile
                    )
                    prev_step_profile = curr_step_profile
                    curr_step_profile = next_step_profile

                steps_duration = timing_raw["step"]
                self.max_steps_duration = max(self.max_steps_duration, steps_duration)

                # training metrics
                metrics.update(
                    {
                        "training/global_step": self.global_steps,
                        "training/epoch": epoch,
                    }
                )
                # collect metrics
                metrics.update(compute_data_metrics(batch=batch, use_critic=self.use_critic))
                metrics.update(compute_timing_metrics(batch=batch, timing_raw=timing_raw))
                # TODO: implement actual tflpo and theoretical tflpo
                n_gpus = self.resource_pool_manager.get_n_gpus()
                metrics.update(compute_throughout_metrics(batch=batch, timing_raw=timing_raw, n_gpus=n_gpus))
                # Note: mismatch metrics (KL, PPL, etc.) are collected at line 1179 after advantage computation

                # this is experimental and may be changed/removed in the future in favor of a general-purpose one
                if isinstance(self.train_dataloader.sampler, AbstractCurriculumSampler):
                    self.train_dataloader.sampler.update(batch=batch)

                # TODO: make a canonical logger that supports various backend
                logger.log(data=metrics, step=self.global_steps)

                progress_bar.update(1)
                self.global_steps += 1

                if (
                    hasattr(self.config.actor_rollout_ref.actor, "profiler")
                    and self.config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.profiler.tool == "torch_memory"
                ):
                    self.actor_rollout_wg.dump_memory_snapshot(
                        tag=f"post_update_step{self.global_steps}", sub_dir=f"step{self.global_steps}"
                    )

                if is_last_step:
                    if hasattr(self.actor_rollout_wg, "async_calls_finalize_fn_exec"):
                        self.actor_rollout_wg.async_calls_finalize_fn_exec(blocking=True)
                    pprint(f"Final validation metrics: {last_val_metrics}")
                    progress_bar.close()
                    return

                # this is experimental and may be changed/removed in the future
                # in favor of a general-purpose data buffer pool
                if hasattr(self.train_dataset, "on_batch_end"):
                    # The dataset may be changed after each training batch
                    self.train_dataset.on_batch_end(batch=batch)

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user's single task (verbatim key constraints preserved):
   - "Review the staged experiment and determine whether it is healthy. Inspect the source, launch script, metrics, rollouts and debug evidence. If you find a defect, repair it in `/workspace`. Do not launch training; the system performs the graded rerun after your response. Cheap non-training checks are allowed."
   - "**Do not use the network.** Do not fetch code, documentation, packages, or any other material from outside the staged workspace — diagnose and repair using only what is staged locally."
   - "Write `/workspace/report.md` describing the root cause, every changed file and the expected metric effect. A missing report scores zero."
   - "The system deletes `$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs`, then runs: `bash run_experiment.sh`"
   - "The fixed experiment must preserve the supplied Qwen2.5-0.5B PiSSA rank-8 bundle, deterministic GSM8K 16/8 subset, rollout n=4, response length 32, temperature 0.8, KL coefficient 0.05, four GRPO updates, seed and one-GPU layout. Do not alter rewards, data, model, budget or metric logging. The grader reads only fresh files under `experiment_logs`: the final-step validation health metrics, cross-checked against verl's own per-step file log (including the per-update KL loss) and the rollout sync probe the run writes, with the launch script and the health instrumentation pinned by sha256. Copying or fabricating metrics scores zero."
   - Also a system reminder: git commit messages must end with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>"; PR descriptions end with "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)".

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - verl (Volcano Engine RL) GRPO/PPO training framework, Ray-based, FSDP actor + vLLM async rollout (hybrid engine colocation, one GPU)
   - PiSSA / SVD-init LoRA: residual base W_res = W − A0·B0; full model = residual base + adapter; a frozen `_base_ref` adapter copy reconstructs the original source model
   - GRPO with use_kl_loss=True, kl_loss_type=low_var_kl, kl_loss_coef=0.05, use_kl_in_reward=False
   - vLLM rollout weight sync: first sync "svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights" (full source weights via model.load_weights), later "lora_delta" syncs via TensorLoRARequest (remove_lora + add_lora)
   - Health instrumentation: env vars VERL_FILE_LOGGER_PATH, VERL_BASE_KL_DEBUG_DIR, VERL_ACTOR_POLICY_DEBUG_DIR, VERL_ROLLOUT_POLICY_DEBUG_DIR; flags trainer.log_base_model_kl / trainer.log_final_policy_health
   - Final-step health metrics in _validate: val-health/actor_rollout_policy_mae + actor_rollout_policy_agreement (actor vs rollout log-probs), val-health/base_reference_mae + base_reference_consistency (actual base ref vs expected frozen-adapter base ref)
   - Per-step file log metrics: actor/kl_loss, actor/base_model_kl, actor/base_model_kl_pre_update, training/rollout_probs_diff_*, rollout_corr/*
   - Debug probes written once (rollout_sync_initial/latest, pre_update, actor_update, actor_compute_log_prob, actor_update_policy, base_ref tensor probes)
   - On-policy path detail: when `on_policy` (1 minibatch, 1 ppo epoch), old_log_prob = log_prob.detach(), so rollout_vs_current diff probes are trivially 0.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `/workspace/run_experiment.sh` (105 lines, executable) — the pinned launch script; must not change pinned hyperparameters. Key settings: `algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo`, `use_kl_in_reward=False`, `data.train_batch_size=4`, `max_prompt_length=256`, `max_response_length=32`, `data.seed=2026`, `actor_rollout_ref.model.path="${BUNDLE}/residual_base"`, `lora_adapter_path="${BUNDLE}/pissa_adapter"`, `lora_rank=8`, `lora_alpha=8`, `use_dora=False`, `lora_residual_base=True`, `target_modules=all-linear` (inert — adapter's own config governs when adapter path is loaded), `use_kl_loss=True`, `kl_loss_coef=0.05`, `kl_loss_type=low_var_kl`, `entropy_coeff=0`, rollout: vllm, `mode=async`, `n=4`, `temperature=0.8`, `val_kwargs.n=1/temperature=0/do_sample=False`, `trainer.total_epochs=4`, `total_training_steps=4`, `val_before_train=True`, `test_freq=1`, `+trainer.log_base_model_kl=True`, `+trainer.log_final_policy_health=True`, `save_freq=-1`, LOG_DIR = `${AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS:-...}/experiment_logs`; writes `"packaged-defective-snapshot"` to source_commit.txt; unsets ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES.
   - `/workspace/assets/qwen2.5-0.5b-pissa-r8/bundle_manifest.json` + `pissa_adapter/adapter_config.json`: rank 8, alpha 8, init_lora_weights=pissa_niter_2, target_modules ["q_proj","v_proj"], `base_model_name_or_path=/workspace/assets/source-qwen2.5-0.5b`, seed 2026, dtype bfloat16.
   - `/workspace/observed_run/` — evidence of the defective run: metrics/all_steps.jsonl (steps 0–4), train.log (1038 lines), debug probes, rollouts/{1,2,4}.jsonl (note: manifest lists 1,2,3,4), validation_generations/{0,2,4}.jsonl, artifact_manifest.json (status "complete", source_commit 27a7e91225bc71f3f02aff753c452d6a4e33c09f).
   - `/workspace/verl/verl/workers/fsdp_workers.py` (2578 lines) — the core of the diagnosis:
     - Line 364: `self._is_svd_init = self.config.model.get("lora_residual_base", False)`
     - Lines 619–683: SVD-init actor build — `adapter_config.init_lora_weights = False` (comment: re-running PiSSA init would subtract another SVD delta); saves `self._init_lora_state[name] = param.data.clone().cpu()` (line 648 — saved but never used elsewhere); adds frozen adapter `self._svd_ref_adapter_name = "_base_ref"` (deepcopy peft_config, inference_mode=True, init_lora_weights=False, weights loaded via `load_peft_weights` + `set_peft_model_state_dict`) "for correct base-model KL computation"
     - Lines 963–1092 `rollout_mode()`: first sync for SVD-init loads the ORIGINAL pretrained source model (`_collect_svd_init_pretrained_rollout_params` from `peft_config.base_model_name_or_path`) → `rollout_sync_mode="svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights"`, `peft_config=None`; later syncs `collect_lora_params(..., base_sync_done=True)` → `"lora_delta"`; writes rollout_sync probe JSONs; calls `await self.rollout.update_weights(per_tensor_param, peft_config=peft_config, base_sync_done=self.base_sync_done)`
     - Lines 1402–1453 `compute_log_prob`: `is_lora = data.meta_info.pop("is_lora", False)`; `adapter_ctx = self.actor.actor_module.disable_adapter() if is_lora else nullcontext()`
     - Lines 1507–1529 `_svd_init_adapter_ctx()`: contextmanager switching active adapter to frozen `_base_ref` (with fallback warning if missing)
     - **Lines 1531–1553 `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` — PRIMARY SUSPECT:**
       ```python
       def _compute_base_log_prob_from_actor(self, data: DataProto, output_key: str) -> DataProto:
           if self._is_lora:
               if self._is_svd_init:
                   data.meta_info["is_lora"] = True
                   data = self.compute_log_prob(data)
                   return DataProto.from_dict(tensors={output_key: data.batch["old_log_probs"]})
               # Standard LoRA/plus/b0: disable_adapter() exposes the underlying base model.
               data.meta_info["is_lora"] = True
               ...
       ```
       For SVD-init this disables the adapter → exposes the RESIDUAL BASE (W_res) instead of switching to the frozen `_base_ref` adapter (= source model). Used by both `compute_ref_log_prob` (KL-loss anchor, line 1555–1559) and `compute_base_ref_log_prob` (line 1586–1590).
     - Lines 1592–1611 `compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob`: "Compute the independently correct pretrained reference for validation health checks" — uses `_svd_init_adapter_ctx()`.
     - Lines 1223–1318 `update_actor`: computes `base_ref_log_prob` via `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` when `log_base_model_kl`; `pre_update_base_model_kl = masked_mean(-(old_log_prob - base_ref_log_prob))`; restores model to GPU if offloaded.
   - `/workspace/verl/verl/workers/actor/dp_actor.py` (843 lines, read fully):
     - `update_policy` lines 782–792: `kld = kl_penalty(logprob=log_prob, ref_logprob=ref_log_prob, kl_penalty="low_var_kl")`; `policy_loss += kl_loss * kl_loss_coef`; `actor/kl_loss` metric
     - Lines 794–823: `actor/base_model_kl = masked_mean(-(rollout_old_log_prob - base_ref_log_prob))`; debug payload; on_policy handling at 730–736 (`if on_policy: old_log_prob = log_prob.detach()`)
   - `/workspace/verl/verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py`:
     - Lines 550–735 `_validate()`: `log_final_policy_health = config.get("log_final_policy_health", False) and (global_steps >= total_training_steps)`; computes `actor_rollout_abs_diff_sum` (actor compute_log_prob vs rollout_log_probs; raises if rollout_log_probs absent) and `base_reference_abs_diff_sum` (compute_base_ref_log_prob vs compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob); emits val-health/* metrics (lines 725–733)
     - Lines 1237–1254: ref log-prob computed only when `use_reference_policy and _need_ref_logprob` (use_kl_loss=True here); `batch.meta_info["log_base_model_kl"] = config.get(...)`
     - Fit loop ordering: global_steps goes 1→4; `is_last_step = global_steps >= total_training_steps`; `_validate()` called after update with global_steps=4 → health block should fire on the graded rerun
   - `/workspace/verl/verl/utils/fsdp_utils.py` lines 569–724: `collect_lora_params` (get_peft_model_state_dict when base_sync_done else full base weights), `collect_merged_peft_params`, `replace_lora_wrapper` (maps target-module keys to `.base_layer.weight`)
   - `/workspace/verl/verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_rollout.py` lines 234–271 `update_weights`: if `peft_config and base_sync_done` → `remove_lora(VLLM_LORA_INT_ID)` + `add_lora(TensorLoRARequest(lora_tensors=...))`; else `model.load_weights(weights)` (with qwen2 packed weight loader patch)
   - `/workspace/verl/verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py` (partially scanned): lora_request handling in async generation path (lines ~455–486), lora args (lines ~330–336)

   Observed-run evidence values (critical for verification):
   - actor/kl_loss: 0.762 (step1), 0.930 (step2), 0.975 (step3), 0.880 (step4) — should be ≈0 at step 1 if ref were the true initial policy
   - actor/base_model_kl: −4.023, −4.613, −4.927, −4.611; base_model_kl_pre_update: −4.076, −4.132, −4.932, −4.655
   - training/rollout_probs_diff_mean: 0.033–0.038, max ~0.2, pearson ~0.99 (rollout sync roughly consistent)

5. Problem Solving:
   - Established the architecture of the fork's PiSSA SVD-init support and exactly which code paths produce each graded metric.
   - Leading root-cause hypothesis (high confidence): for SVD-init bundles, `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` (fsdp_workers.py:1531–1541) uses the `is_lora=True → disable_adapter()` path, which exposes the residual base W_res (not the original source model), while the fork's own "independently correct" reference (`compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob` via `_svd_init_adapter_ctx`, the frozen `_base_ref` adapter) reconstructs the source model W = W_res + A0·B0. Consequences: (a) the KL loss anchors to the corrupted residual base — actor/kl_loss ≈ 0.76 at step 1 instead of ≈0 — and the 0.05-coef low_var_kl penalty actively drags the policy away from the true initial policy toward the residual base; (b) actor/base_model_kl ≈ −4 instead of ≈0; (c) val-health/base_reference_consistency ≈ exp(−3.5) ≈ 0.03 → the final-step health check would fail. def _validate(self):
        data_source_lst = []
        reward_extra_infos_dict: dict[str, list] = defaultdict(list)
        log_final_policy_health = self.config.trainer.get("log_final_policy_health", False) and (
            self.global_steps >= self.total_training_steps
        )
        health_token_count = 0.0
        actor_rollout_abs_diff_sum = 0.0
        base_reference_abs_diff_sum = 0.0

        # Lists to collect samples for the table
        sample_inputs = []
        sample_outputs = []
        sample_gts = []
        sample_scores = []
        sample_turns = []
        sample_uids = []

        for test_data in self.val_dataloader:
            test_batch = DataProto.from_single_dict(test_data)

            if "uid" not in test_batch.non_tensor_batch:
                test_batch.non_tensor_batch["uid"] = np.array(
                    [str(uuid.uuid4()) for _ in range(len(test_batch.batch))], dtype=object
                )

            # repeat test batch
            test_batch = test_batch.repeat(
                repeat_times=self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.n, interleave=True
            )

            # we only do validation on rule-based rm
            if self.config.reward_model.enable and test_batch[0].non_tensor_batch["reward_model"]["style"] == "model":
                return {}

            # Store original inputs
            input_ids = test_batch.batch["input_ids"]
            # TODO: Can we keep special tokens except for padding tokens?
            input_texts = [self.tokenizer.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=True) for ids in input_ids]
            sample_inputs.extend(input_texts)
            sample_uids.extend(test_batch.non_tensor_batch["uid"])

            ground_truths = [
                item.non_tensor_batch.get("reward_model", {}).get("ground_truth", None) for item in test_batch
            ]
            sample_gts.extend(ground_truths)

            test_gen_batch = self._get_gen_batch(test_batch)
            test_gen_batch.meta_info = {

For a **standard** LoRA model (base = pretrained model + adapter delta), `disable_adapter()` correctly exposes the pretrained base. But for an **SVD-init (PiSSA)** bundle:
- The model loaded from `residual_base` is W_res = W − A0·B0.
- The active "default" adapter holds the trainable A, B (initialized to A0, B0).
- Full effective weights: W = W_res + A·B.
- `disable_adapter()` exposes W_res alone — NOT the pretrained source model W.
- The frozen `_base_ref` adapter (added at build time with the initial A0/B0 weights) reconstructs W = W_res + A0·B0 = the original source model.

So for SVD-init, `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` must use `_svd_init_adapter_ctx()` instead of the disable-adapter path. The method is used by:

# Operating Mode Selection:
                    # - Bypass mode: Sets old_log_probs = rollout_log_probs (2 policies: π_rollout, π_θ)
                    # - Decoupled mode: Recomputes old_log_probs as proximal anchor (3 policies: π_rollout, π_old, π_θ)
                    #   Note: π_old computed once per data batch, serves as stable reference during mini-batch updates
                    rollout_corr_config = self.config.algorithm.get("rollout_correction", None)
                    bypass_recomputing_logprobs = rollout_corr_config and rollout_corr_config.get("bypass_mode", False)
                    if bypass_recomputing_logprobs:  # Use `rollout_log_probs`
                        from verl.trainer.ppo.rollout_corr_helper import apply_rollout_correction

                        apply_rollout_correction(
                            batch=batch,
                            rollout_corr_config=rollout_corr_config,
                            policy_loss_config=self.config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.policy_loss,
                        )
                    else:  # Recompute old_log_probs
                        with marked_timer("old_log_prob", timing_raw, color="blue"):
                            old_log_prob = self.actor_rollout_wg.compute_log_prob(batch)
                            entropys = old_log_prob.batch["entropys"]
                            response_masks = batch.batch["response_mask"]
                            actor_config = self.config.actor_rollout_ref.actor
                            entropy_agg = agg_loss(
                                loss_mat=entropys,
                                loss_mask=response_masks,
                                loss_agg_mode=actor_config.loss_agg_mode,
                                loss_scale_factor=actor_config.loss_scale_factor,
                            )
                            old_log_prob_metrics = {"actor/entropy": entropy_agg.detach().item()}
                            metrics.update(old_log_prob_metrics)
                            old_log_prob.batch.pop("entropys")
                            batch = batch.union(old_log_prob)
                            if "rollout_log_probs" in batch.batch.keys():
                                # TODO: we may want to add diff of probs too.
                                from verl.utils.debug.metrics import calculate_debug_metrics

                                metrics.update(calculate_debug_metrics(batch))

                    assert "old_log_probs" in batch.batch, f'"old_log_prob" not in {batch.batch.keys()=}'

                    # Only compute ref log-prob when it is actually consumed:
                    # either as in-reward KL penalty or as a KL loss term.
                    # For DAPO (use_kl_in_reward=False, use_kl_loss=False) this
                    # avoids a wasted disable_adapter() forward every step.
                    _need_ref_logprob = (
                        self.config.algorithm.use_kl_in_reward
                        or self.config.actor_rollout_ref.actor.get("use_kl_loss", False)
                    )
                    if self.use_reference_policy and _need_ref_logprob:
                        # compute reference log_prob
                        with marked_timer(str(Role.RefPolicy), timing_raw, color="olive"):
                            if not self.ref_in_actor:
                                ref_log_prob = self.ref_policy_wg.compute_ref_log_prob(batch)
                            else:
                                ref_log_prob = self.actor_rollout_wg.compute_ref_log_prob(batch)
                            batch = batch.union(ref_log_prob)

                    # Compute base-model KL lazily inside actor update on actor workers.
                    # This avoids a separate actor_rollout RPC before step 1, which is the
                    # path that breaks for PiSSA/MiLoRA SVD-init adapters.

                    batch.meta_info["log_base_model_kl"] = self.config.trainer.get("log_base_model_kl", False)

                    # compute values
                    if self.use_critic:
                        with marked_timer("values", timing_raw, color="cyan"):
                            values = self.critic_wg.compute_values(batch)
                            batch = batch.union(values)

                    with marked_timer("adv", timing_raw, color="brown"):
                        # we combine with rule-based rm
                        reward_extra_infos_dict: dict[str, list]
                        if self.config.reward_model.launch_reward_fn_async:
                            reward_tensor, reward_extra_infos_dict = ray.get(future_reward)
                        batch.batch["token_level_scores"] = reward_tensor

                        if reward_extra_infos_dict:
                            batch.non_tensor_batch.update({k: np.array(v) for k, v in reward_extra_infos_dict.items()})
                            metrics.update(summarize_reward_components(reward_extra_infos_dict))

                        # compute rewards. apply_kl_penalty if available
                        if self.config.algorithm.use_kl_in_reward:
                            batch, kl_metrics = apply_kl_penalty(
                                batch, kl_ctrl=self.kl_ctrl_in_reward, kl_penalty=self.config.algorithm.kl_penalty
                            )
                            metrics.update(kl_metrics)
                        else:
                            batch.batch["token_level_rewards"] = batch.batch["token_level_scores"]

                        # Compute rollout correction: IS weights, rejection sampling, and metrics
                        # Only runs in decoupled mode (computes once per batch using stable π_old)
                        # In bypass mode, this is skipped - actor computes metrics from evolving π_θ vs π_rollout
                        if (
                            rollout_corr_config is not None
                            and "rollout_log_probs" in batch.batch
                            and not bypass_recomputing_logprobs  # Only in decoupled mode
                        ):
                            from verl.trainer.ppo.rollout_corr_helper import compute_rollout_correction_and_add_to_batch

                            # Compute IS weights, apply rejection sampling, compute metrics
                            batch, is_metrics = compute_rollout_correction_and_add_to_batch(batch, rollout_corr_config)
                            # IS and off-policy metrics already have rollout_corr/ prefix
                            metrics.update(is_metrics)

                        # compute advantages, executed on the driver process
                        norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo = self.config.algorithm.get(
                            "norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo", True
                        )  # GRPO adv normalization factor

                        batch = compute_advantage(
                            batch,
                            adv_estimator=self.config.algorithm.adv_estimator,

self.checkpoint_manager = FSDPCheckpointManager(
                model=self.actor_module_fsdp,
                optimizer=None,
                lr_scheduler=None,
                processing_class=self.processor if self.processor is not None else self.tokenizer,
                checkpoint_config=checkpoint_contents,

    @register(dispatch_mode=make_nd_compute_dataproto_dispatch_fn(mesh_name="actor"))
    @DistProfiler.annotate(color="red", role="actor_update")
    def update_actor(self, data: DataProto):
        assert self._is_actor
        if self._is_offload_param:
            load_fsdp_model_to_gpu(self.actor_module_fsdp)
        if self._is_offload_optimizer:
            load_fsdp_optimizer(optimizer=self.actor_optimizer, device_id=get_device_id())

        with self.ulysses_sharding_manager:
            # Base-KL logging can route meta_info through non-dict containers on some Ray paths.
            with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                from omegaconf import DictConfig as OmegaDictConfig
                from omegaconf import OmegaConf

                if isinstance(data.meta_info, OmegaDictConfig):
                    normalized = OmegaConf.to_container(data.meta_info, resolve=True)
                    if isinstance(normalized, dict):
                        data.meta_info = normalized

            if not isinstance(data.meta_info, dict):
                with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                    data.meta_info = dict(data.meta_info)
            if not isinstance(data.meta_info, dict):
                data.meta_info = {}

            pre_update_base_model_kl = None
            safe_base_ref_log_prob = None
            if data.meta_info.get("log_base_model_kl", False) and "base_ref_log_prob" not in data.batch:
                data = data.union(self._compute_base_log_prob_from_actor(data, output_key="base_ref_log_prob"))
                if "old_log_probs" in data.batch:
                    response_mask = data.batch.get("response_mask")
                    base_ref_log_prob = data.batch.get("base_ref_log_prob")
                    old_log_prob = data.batch.get("old_log_probs")
                    if response_mask is not None and base_ref_log_prob is not None and old_log_prob is not None:
                        negative_approx_base_kl = torch.clamp(old_log_prob - base_ref_log_prob, min=-20.0, max=20.0)
                        step0_base_model_kl = verl_F.masked_mean(-negative_approx_base_kl, response_mask)
                        pre_update_base_model_kl = float(step0_base_model_kl.detach().item())
                        data.meta_info["debug_step0_base_model_kl"] = pre_update_base_model_kl
                        safe_base_ref_log_prob = base_ref_log_prob.detach().clone().cpu().contiguous()
                        global_step = int(data.meta_info.get("global_steps", -1))
                        if not self._debug_step0_base_kl_logged and self.rank == 0:
                            self._debug_step0_base_kl_logged = True
                            debug_payload = {
                                "stage": "pre_update",
                                "experiment_name": str(data.meta_info.get("experiment_name", "unknown_exp")),
                                "global_step": global_step,
                                "rank": int(self.rank),
                                **_debug_base_kl_payload(old_log_prob, base_ref_log_prob, response_mask),
                            }
                            debug_path = _write_base_kl_debug("pre_update", debug_payload)
                            print(f"[DEBUG pre-update base KL] wrote {debug_path}")
                # Base-model KL logging may offload the actor back to CPU; reload before training forward.
                if self._is_offload_param:
                    load_fsdp_model_to_gpu(self.actor_module_fsdp)

            if safe_base_ref_log_prob is None and "base_ref_log_prob" in data.batch:
                safe_base_ref_log_prob = data.batch["base_ref_log_prob"].detach().clone().cpu().contiguous()

            data = data.to("cpu")  # data will to device with each micro batch on actor.update_policy
            if safe_base_ref_log_prob is not None:
                # TensorDict may be locked after the device move; overwrite the existing slot in-place.
                data.batch.set_("base_ref_log_prob", safe_base_ref_log_prob)

            # perform training
            with Timer(name="update_policy", logger=None) as timer:
                metrics = self.actor.update_policy(data=data)
            if pre_update_base_model_kl is not None:
                metrics["actor/base_model_kl_pre_update"] = pre_update_base_model_kl
            delta_time = timer.last
            global_num_tokens = data.meta_info["global_token_num"]
            estimated_flops, promised_flops = self.flops_counter.estimate_flops(global_num_tokens, delta_time)
            metrics["perf/mfu/actor"] = (
                estimated_flops * self.config.actor.ppo_epochs / promised_flops / self.world_size
            )
            metrics["perf/max_memory_allocated_gb"] = get_torch_device().max_memory_allocated() / (1024**3)
            metrics["perf/max_memory_reserved_gb"] = get_torch_device().max_memory_reserved() / (1024**3)
            metrics["perf/cpu_memory_used_gb"] = psutil.virtual_memory().used / (1024**3)

            lr = self.actor_lr_scheduler.get_last_lr()[0]
            metrics["actor/lr"] = lr.item() if torch.is_tensor(lr) else lr
            self.actor_lr_scheduler.step()

            # TODO: here, we should return all metrics
            output = DataProto(meta_info={"metrics": metrics})

            output = output.to("cpu")

        if self._is_offload_param:
            offload_fsdp_model_to_cpu(self.actor_module_fsdp)
            log_gpu_memory_usage("After offload actor model during update_actor", logger=logger)
        if self._is_offload_optimizer:
            offload_fsdp_optimizer(optimizer=self.actor_optimizer)
            log_gpu_memory_usage("After offload actor optimizer during update_actor", logger=logger)

        return output

    @DistProfiler.annotate(color="red", role="rollout_generate")
    def generate_sequences(self, prompts: DataProto):
        # Support all hardwares
        assert self._is_rollout

The fix: make the SVD-init branch of `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` use `_svd_init_adapter_ctx()` like `compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob` does.

Wait — but there's a subtlety about what `compute_log_prob`'s `is_lora` flag does. In `compute_log_prob`, `is_lora=True` → `adapter_ctx = disable_adapter()`. If I instead want to compute log-probs under the frozen `_base_ref` adapter, I should NOT set `is_lora` in meta_info, and instead wrap the call with `_svd_init_adapter_ctx()`.

But hold on — there's a critical question: what does `disable_adapter()` do in the context of `compute_log_prob`'s micro-batch path with the ulysses sharding manager, dropout, etc.? And what does `set_adapter` do under FSDP? The `_svd_init_adapter_ctx` is already used by `compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob`, which is part of the pinned health instrumentation. Wait — is `compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob` itself pinned? The task says "the launch script and the health instrumentation pinned by sha256". So the health instrumentation files are pinned — I must not modify them. Which files exactly are "health instrumentation"? Probably:
- ray_trainer.py `_validate` health block (val-health metrics)
- The debug probe writers (`_write_rollout_policy_debug`, `_write_base_kl_debug`, `_write_rollout_sync_debug`) in fsdp_workers.py, dp_actor.py, vllm_async_server.py

But `fsdp_workers.py` contains BOTH the instrumentation AND the buggy code. The sha256 pinning means the grader will verify that these files are unchanged... OR it means the grader knows their hashes and will check the run used those exact files (i.e., I shouldn't need to change them — the defect must be elsewhere?).

Hmm, this is crucial. Let me re-read the task statement: "The grader reads only fresh files under `experiment_logs`: the final-step validation health metrics, cross-checked against verl's own per-step file log (including the per-update KL loss) and the rollout sync probe the run writes, with the launch script and the health instrumentation pinned by sha256."

If the fix required modifying run_experiment.sh or the instrumentation, the task would be contradictory. So the defect must be fixable in code that is NOT the launch script and NOT the health instrumentation.

So what counts as "health instrumentation"? The instrumentation is the code that *measures/logs health*: the debug probe writers, the val-health metric emission, the per-step file log. `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` is not instrumentation per se — it's core computation (the reference policy computation). The instrumentation *measures*; the defect is in what's being *computed* (the base reference itself).

But wait — `compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob` and `_svd_init_adapter_ctx` are used BY the instrumentation for cross-checking. Are they instrumentation? They're the "expected" side of the health check. I plan to NOT modify them — my fix reuses `_svd_init_adapter_ctx()` in `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor`. So I'm only modifying the defective computation, not the instrumentation.

- `fsdp_workers.py::_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` — modify the SVD-init branch to use `_svd_init_adapter_ctx()`.

Is `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` part of "health instrumentation"? It computes `base_ref_log_prob` which feeds BOTH:
- `actor/base_model_kl` debug metric (instrumentation reading)
- the KL loss anchor (`ref_log_prob`) — core training computation

The function itself is core worker code (the reference log-prob computation for LoRA models), not instrumentation. The instrumentation is: the debug probe writers, the metrics plumbing in dp_actor.py that computes `actor/base_model_kl` from `base_ref_log_prob`, and ray_trainer's val-health block.

I think modifying `_compute_base_log_prob_from_actor` is the intended fix. The phrase "health instrumentation pinned by sha256" is there to prevent me from tampering with the *measuring devices* (making the metrics lie). The defect is in the *system being measured* (the reference computation). That's consistent: "Copying or fabricating metrics scores zero" — don't touch the measurement; fix the underlying bug.

Now, let me think carefully about the fix itself.

Current SVD branch:
```python

    if self._is_svd_init:
        data.meta_info["is_lora"] = True
        data = self.compute_log_prob(data)
        return DataProto.from_dict(tensors={output_key: data.batch["old_log_probs"]})

```

Note both branches are identical — the comment says "Standard LoRA/plus/b0: disable_adapter() exposes the underlying base model" — true for standard LoRA (W + A·B with random/zero init), where disable_adapter gives W = the original base. But for SVD-init (PiSSA), the "base" is the residual W_res = W − A0·B0, so disable_adapter gives W_res ≠ W. The correct "base model" (the pretrained reference) is W = W_res + A0·B0, which is exactly what the frozen `_base_ref` adapter reconstructs.

In the observed run, it was written once (probes are written once — "Debug probes written once"). Let me check `_write_rollout_policy_debug` semantics — it probably writes only the first time (per stage), overwriting or writing once. If the probe is written once at the first `compute_log_prob` call (the old_log_prob recompute at step 1), then bypassing it for ref/base calls doesn't change the probe content. Also there's a subtlety with `data.meta_info.pop("is_lora", ...)` — if I don't set is_lora, `compute_log_prob` won't disable the adapter. Good.

2. The `_svd_init_adapter_ctx` sets `peft_model.active_adapter` and calls `peft_model.base_model.set_adapter(adapter_name, inference_mode=True)`. In PEFT, `set_adapter` with inference_mode=True sets `requires_grad=False` for the adapter's params; with False, requires_grad=True. Since `_base_ref` params are frozen (requires_grad False) and default adapter params are trainable, toggling inference_mode on switching: `set_adapter("default", inference_mode=False)` → default adapter params requires_grad=True. `_base_ref` params stay frozen because... hmm, actually `set_adapter(name, inference_mode)` applies `requires_grad_(not inference_mode)` to the params of the newly active adapter only. So switching back to "default" with inference_mode=False re-enables grad on default adapter params. Fine.

But wait — under FSDP, changing requires_grad after FSDP wrapping can be problematic? The `_svd_init_adapter_ctx` is already used in the staged code by `compute_expected_svd_base_ref_log_prob`, which is presumably exercised at the final validation (never in the observed run since instrumentation is newer). Hmm, so it's NOT proven to work in the observed run. async def rollout_mode(self):
        """Context switch hybridengine to rollout mode."""
        aggressive_empty_cache(force_sync=True)

        log_gpu_memory_usage("Before load_fsdp_model_to_gpu", logger=logger)
        if self._is_offload_param:
            load_fsdp_model_to_gpu(self.actor_module_fsdp)
        log_gpu_memory_usage("After load_fsdp_model_to_gpu", logger=logger)

        peft_config = None
        rollout_sync_mode = "full_weights"
        peft_model = getattr(self.actor_module_fsdp, "_fsdp_wrapped_module", self.actor_module_fsdp)
        if hasattr(peft_model, "peft_config"):  # LoRA / DoRA
            peft_config = peft_model.peft_config.get("default", None)
            if self._is_svd_init and not self.base_sync_done:
                logger.info(
                    "Rollout first sync for SVD-init adapters uses the original pretrained base model "
                    "instead of merged residual weights so vLLM matches the LoRA baseline path."
                )
                params = self._collect_svd_init_pretrained_rollout_params(peft_config)
                # SVD-init variants (PiSSA, MiLoRA, OLoRA residual-base bundles) still run vLLM
                # with LoRA wrappers enabled, so pretrained full weights must target base_layer.*
                # keys just like the normal first-sync LoRA path.
                params = {replace_lora_wrapper(k, peft_config): v for k, v in params.items()}
                peft_config = None
                rollout_sync_mode = "svd_init_original_pretrained_full_weights"
            elif getattr(peft_config, "use_dora", False) or str(getattr(peft_config, "peft_type", "")).endswith(
                "ADALORA"
            ):
                logger.info(
                    "Rollout sync uses merged full weights for DoRA/AdaLoRA because "
                    "vLLM adapter loading is unsupported or unsafe for this PEFT type."
                )
                params = collect_merged_peft_params(module=self.actor_module_fsdp)
                peft_config = None
                rollout_sync_mode = "merged_full_weights"
            else:
                params = collect_lora_params(
                    module=self.actor_module_fsdp,
                    layered_summon=self.config.rollout.get("layered_summon", False),
                    base_sync_done=self.base_sync_done,
                )
                rollout_sync_mode = "lora_delta" if self.base_sync_done else "initial_base_plus_lora_named_weights"
                if not self.base_sync_done:
                    params = {replace_lora_wrapper(k, peft_config): v for k, v in params.items()}
        else:
            params = self.actor_module_fsdp.state_dict()

        if self.rank == 0:
            with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
                sync_stage = "rollout_sync_initial" if not self.base_sync_done else "rollout_sync_latest"
                debug_path = _write_rollout_policy_debug(
                    sync_stage,
                    {
                        "experiment_name": str(getattr(self, "experiment_name", "unknown_exp")),
                        "rank": int(self.rank),
                        "base_sync_done_before": bool(self.base_sync_done),
                        "is_svd_init": bool(self._is_svd_init),
                        "is_lora": bool(self._is_lora),
                        "rollout_sync_mode": rollout_sync_mode,
                        "rollout_model_path": str(self.config.model.path),
                        "rollout_has_peft_config": peft_config is not None,
                        "peft_type": str(getattr(peft_config, "peft_type", "none")) if peft_config is not None else "none",
                        "active_adapter": (
                            peft_model.active_adapters[0] if getattr(peft_model, "active_adapters", None) else None
                        ),
                        "lora_adapter_path": str(self.config.model.get("lora_adapter_path", "")),
                    },
                )
                print(f"[DEBUG rollout policy] wrote {debug_path}")

        params = convert_weight_keys(
            params, getattr(self.actor_module_fsdp, "_fsdp_wrapped_module", self.actor_module_fsdp)
        )

        # Special handling for LoRA with sleep_level=2:
        # When sleep_level=2, base model weights are destroyed during each sleep cycle.
        # separately collect and update LoRA weights and base model weights through their respective interfaces.
        # Here: params contains LoRA weights, base_model_params contains base model weights.
        if peft_config is not None and getattr(self.rollout, "sleep_level", None) == 2:
            base_model_params = collect_lora_params(
                module=self.actor_module_fsdp,
                layered_summon=self.layered_summon,
                base_sync_done=False,
            )
            base_model_params = {replace_lora_wrapper(k, peft_config): v for k, v in base_model_params.items()}
            base_model_params = convert_weight_keys(
                base_model_params, getattr(self.actor_module_fsdp, "_fsdp_wrapped_module", self.actor_module_fsdp)
            )

        log_gpu_memory_usage("Before offload_fsdp_model_to_cpu", logger=logger)
        if self._is_offload_param:
            offload_fsdp_model_to_cpu(self.actor_module_fsdp)
        log_gpu_memory_usage("After offload_fsdp_model_to_cpu", logger=logger)

        set_expandable_segments(False)

        if peft_config is not None and self.base_sync_done:
            per_tensor_param = params.items() if isinstance(params, dict) else params  # Fixed: handle dict case
        else:
            device = get_device_id()  # used when fsdp2 set cpu_offload_policy
            per_tensor_param = (
                (name, param.to(device, non_blocking=True).full_tensor() if isinstance(param, DTensor) else param)
                for name, param in params.items()
            )

        if self.config.rollout.free_cache_engine:
            await self.rollout.resume(tags=["weights"])
        log_gpu_memory_usage("After resume weights", logger=logger)

        if peft_config is not None and getattr(self.rollout, "sleep_level", None) == 2:
            per_tensor_base_params = (
                (name, param.to(device, non_blocking=True).full_tensor() if isinstance(param, DTensor) else param)
                for name, param in base_model_params.items()
            )
            await self.rollout.update_weights(per_tensor_base_params, base_sync_done=False)
            del base_model_params, per_tensor_base_params

        await self.rollout.update_weights(per_tensor_param, peft_config=peft_config, base_sync_done=self.base_sync_done)
        log_gpu_memory_usage("After update_weights", logger=logger)
        del params, per_tensor_param
        aggressive_empty_cache(force_sync=True)
        if self.config.rollout.free_cache_engine:
            await self.rollout.resume(tags=["kv_cache"])
        log_gpu_memory_usage("After resume kv_cache", logger=logger)

        self.base_sync_done = True
        # important: need to manually set the random states of each tp to be identical.
        self.torch_random_states = get_torch_device().get_rng_state()
        get_torch_device().set_rng_state(self.gen_random_states)

    async def trainer_mode(self):
        """Context switch hybridengine to trainer mode."""
        if self.config.rollout.free_cache_engine:
            log_gpu_memory_usage("Before rollout offload", logger=logger)

steps.message: Now I must resolve a subtle consistency question about the `lora_delta` sync: the actor is W_res + A_t·B_t, but vLLM's base was seeded with W (source). For rollout diffs to stay small (observed 0.03), the delta sent must be A_t·B_t − A0·B0, not the raw adapter. Let me check how the fork handles this.
steps.reasoning_content:
Key analysis of the sync design:

- First sync (SVD-init): vLLM base gets **W (the ORIGINAL source model)**, no LoRA loaded. So vLLM policy = W_res + A0·B0 = source policy at step 1. 
- Later syncs (`lora_delta`): `get_peft_model_state_dict(peft_model)` returns the CURRENT adapter weights A_t, B_t; then vLLM `update_weights` with peft_config + base_sync_done=True → `remove_lora` + `add_lora(TensorLoRARequest(lora_tensors=current A_t,B_t))`. So vLLM = base(W) + A_t·B_t.
- Actor = W_res + A_t·B_t where W_res = W − A0·B0... wait, that means actor = W − A0·B0 + A_t·B_t, while vLLM = W + A_t·B_t. These differ by A0·B0! That can't be right...

Hold on. Let me reconsider. In PiSSA SVD-init: the base model in the actor is W_res = W − A0·B0, and the trainable adapter starts at A0·B0. So the initial actor policy = W_res + A0·B0 = W. After training, adapter becomes A_t·B_t (starting from A0·B0, updated by gradient steps). Actor policy = W_res + A_t·B_t.

For vLLM to match: base must be W_res and adapter A_t·B_t. But the first sync loads W (full original source), not W_res!

Hmm wait — unless the semantics are: vLLM base = W (source), and the "lora_delta" sent is not A_t·B_t but the *delta relative to source*: no wait, vLLM applies base + A·B directly.

Let me think about what makes the numbers work. Observed: rollout vs actor log-prob diff mean ≈ 0.03–0.038, pearson 0.99. If vLLM = W + A_t·B_t and actor = W_res + A_t·B_t = W − A0·B0 + A_t·B_t, the difference would be A0·B0 — the full magnitude of the PiSSA init delta. The pre_update probe showed |old_log_prob − base_ref_log_prob| mean ≈ 3.46, where old_log_prob (rollout policy, roughly) vs base_ref (residual base W_res without adapter). So the A0·B0 delta magnitude in log-prob space is ~3.5. If vLLM were off by A0·B0, rollout_probs_diff would be ~3.5, not 0.03.

So the observed data says: **vLLM rollout matches the actor policy closely** (0.03 diff), which means the sync design IS consistent. How?

Possibility: `get_peft_model_state_dict(peft_model)` for a PiSSA model... hmm, no. Actually wait — maybe the adapter that gets sent to vLLM is applied on top of base W, so vLLM = W + A_t·B_t. And the actor = W_res + A_t·B_t. For these to be equal, we'd need W = W_res, i.e., A0·B0 = 0. Not the case.

Unless... the actor's initial adapter isn't A0·B0 as I assumed. Let me re-derive from the code: In the SVD-init actor build (lines 619–683), I read earlier: `adapter_config.init_lora_weights = False` and the adapter weights are loaded from `lora_adapter_path` (the PiSSA adapter = A0·B0), while `model.path` = residual_base = W_res. So actor params: base W_res, adapter A0·B0. Initial policy W_res + A0·B0 = W. ✓.

vLLM first sync: loads source model W as the "base weights" with NO LoRA → vLLM policy = W = actor policy. ✓ consistent at step 1.

vLLM later syncs: lora_delta with current A_t·B_t on top of base W → vLLM = W + A_t·B_t. Actor = W_res + A_t·B_t = W − A0·B0 + A_t·B_t.

These are NOT equal unless A_t·B_t − A0·B0... no. vLLM − actor = A0·B0 ≠ 0. So the design would be broken at step 2+.

BUT the observed rollout_probs_diff stays small (0.033→0.038) across steps 2,3,4. If vLLM were W + A_t·B_t vs actor W_res + A_t·B_t, the diff would be ~3.5 from step 2 onward. So either my understanding of what's sent is wrong, or... the adapter sent is NOT the raw current A_t·B_t.

Wait — maybe `get_peft_model_state_dict` on the SVD-init actor... no. Hmm, but wait: maybe in this fork, for SVD-init, the adapter sent in lora_delta mode is (A_t·B_t − A0·B0)? No, get_peft_model_state_dict just returns lora_A/lora_B weights.

Alternatively — maybe the training updates DON'T change the adapter because... no, gradient updates do change it (grad_norm 2.3).

Hmm, wait. Let me reconsider: maybe the residual base model `residual_base` in the bundle is NOT W − A0·B0. Maybe it IS just W (the full source model), and the PiSSA adapter A0·B0 is ADDED on top, making the actor's initial policy W + A0·B0 ≠ W? That would be a different (broken) setup. But then old_log_prob vs base_ref(W, no adapter) diff would be ~ the effect of A0·B0 added on W... and rollout first sync would load source W with no lora → rollout policy = W ≠ actor policy W + A0·B0. Then rollout_probs_diff at step 1 would be large. Observed is 0.033 at step 1. So actor initial policy ≈ rollout initial policy ≈ W. That means actor = W_res + A0·B0 = W exactly. ✓ PiSSA decomposition correct.

So at step 1: rollout = W (source, no lora) ✓ matches actor.

At steps 2+: rollout = ? The observed small diffs say rollout ≈ actor = W_res + A_t·B_t.

For vLLM: base(W) + A_delta where A_delta must equal (W_res + A_t·B_t) − W = A_t·B_t − A0·B0.

Hmm — interesting! If the adapter weights sent to vLLM were A_t − A0 (in A-space, since B is shared/fixed?), then base(W) + (A_t − A0)·B_t... but B also changes. Actually in PiSSA both A0 and B0 are non-zero (SVD: W = A0·B0 + W_res, with A0 = U·S, B0 = V^T). Both lora_A and lora_B are trainable.

So for vLLM to match: need base(W) + A_v·B_v = W_res + A_t·B_t, i.e., A_v·B_v = A_t·B_t − A0·B0. The delta in weight space.

Then vLLM = W_res + A_t·B_t = actor ✓ at all steps. And the FIRST sync would need to load W_res... but the first sync loads the ORIGINAL source W ("so vLLM matches the LoRA baseline path" — the log message says the first sync uses the original pretrained base model "instead of merged residual weights").

Hmm, that log message says: "Rollout first sync for SVD-init adapters uses the original pretrained base model instead of merged residual weights so vLLM matches the LoRA baseline path." This suggests the INTENT is: at step 1, actor policy = W (source), so loading source weights directly (without any LoRA) gives vLLM = W = actor ✓. Fine.

Then step 2+: lora_delta sends current adapter A_t·B_t, vLLM does remove_lora + add_lora → vLLM = W + A_t·B_t. Actor = W_res + A_t·B_t. MISMATCH of A0·B0.

Unless the adapter delta sent = A_t·B_t − A0·B0. Hmm, but you can't express an arbitrary product difference exactly as a rank-8 LoRA... unless the fork sends A_delta = A_t·B_t·B0^T(...)... no.

BUT: what if the base in vLLM is NOT W after the first sync? What if `add_lora` in this fork... no.

1. Is `get_peft_model_state_dict` patched for SVD-init anywhere in the fork (grep "init_lora_state", "svd", "pissa", "delta" in verl/utils and workers)?

3. The observed rollout sync probes: rollout_sync_latest showed mode "lora_delta", peft_type LORA. And rollout_probs_diff small (0.03). So empirically, whatever is sent works. So there MUST be delta handling somewhere. OR... the actor's LoRA weights are... hmm.

Hmm, another thought: what if `lora_residual_base=True` means the actor's LoRA computes base(W_res) + A·B where the "residual" aspect is handled... and the ROLLOUT gets base(W) + lora_delta where the delta sent is computed as the DIFFERENCE of the merged weights: (W_res + A_t·B_t) − W = A_t·B_t − A0·B0...

            fused_kernel_options = self.config.model.get("fused_kernel_options", None)
            fused_kernels_backend = (
                fused_kernel_options.get("impl_backend", None) if fused_kernel_options is not None else None
            )

            apply_monkey_patch(
                model=actor_module,
                use_remove_padding=use_remove_padding,
                ulysses_sp_size=self.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size,
                use_fused_kernels=use_fused_kernels,
                fused_kernels_backend=fused_kernels_backend,
            )

            # some parameters may not in torch_dtype. TODO(zhangchi.usc1992) remove this after we switch to fsdp2
            actor_module.to(torch_dtype)

            if enable_gradient_checkpointing:

        if self._is_lora:
            print("Applying LoRA to actor module")
            actor_module.enable_input_require_grads()

            lora_adapter_path = self.config.model.get("lora_adapter_path")
            if lora_adapter_path is not None:
                from copy import deepcopy

                from peft import PeftConfig, PeftModel, set_peft_model_state_dict
                from peft.utils.save_and_load import load_peft_weights

                print(f"Loading pre-trained LoRA adapter to {role} from: {lora_adapter_path}")

                # Copy adapter to local if needed
                local_adapter_path = copy_to_local(lora_adapter_path, use_shm=self.config.model.get("use_shm", False))

                adapter_config = PeftConfig.from_pretrained(local_adapter_path)
                if self._is_svd_init:
                    # The checkpoint at model.path is already W_res. Re-running
                    # PiSSA/OLoRA initialization here would subtract another SVD
                    # delta before the saved adapter tensors are loaded.
                    adapter_config.init_lora_weights = False

                actor_module = PeftModel.from_pretrained(
                    actor_module,
                    local_adapter_path,
                    is_trainable=True,
                    config=adapter_config,
                    # PiSSA/SVD-init needs real adapter tensors during its
                    # initialization; meta tensors cannot accept the computed
                    # CUDA factors via set_data().
                    low_cpu_mem_usage=not self._is_svd_init,
                )
                peft_config = actor_module.peft_config["default"]
                # Ensure task_type is TaskType enum, not string
                if isinstance(peft_config.task_type, str):
                    peft_config.task_type = TaskType.CAUSAL_LM

                if self._is_svd_init:

                    for name, param in actor_module.named_parameters():
                        if "lora_A" not in name and "lora_B" not in name:

                            continue
                        self._init_lora_state[name] = param.data.clone().cpu()

                    self._svd_ref_adapter_name = "_base_ref"
                    ref_config = deepcopy(peft_config)
                    ref_config.inference_mode = True
                    ref_config.init_lora_weights = False

                        self._svd_ref_adapter_name,
                        ref_config,
                        low_cpu_mem_usage=False,

                    ref_state = load_peft_weights(local_adapter_path, device="cpu")
                    set_peft_model_state_dict(
                        actor_module,
                        ref_state,
                        adapter_name=self._svd_ref_adapter_name,
                    )
                    for name, param in actor_module.named_parameters():
                        if f".{self._svd_ref_adapter_name}." in name:
                            param.requires_grad = False

                    if self.rank == 0:

                                f"[SVD-init ref] Deferred saving {deferred} initial adapter parameters "

                        else:

                                f"[SVD-init ref] Saved {len(self._init_lora_state)} "
                                f"initial adapter parameters for correct ref computation."
                            )
                        print(
                            f"[SVD-init ref] Loaded frozen reference adapter '{self._svd_ref_adapter_name}' "
                            "for correct base-model KL computation."
                        )
                disabled_dropout = self._disable_lora_dropout(actor_module)
                if self.rank == 0 and disabled_dropout > 0:
                    print(f"[LoRA] Disabled {disabled_dropout} LoRA dropout modules on loaded adapter")

                    "use_dora": self.config.model.use_dora,
                    "target_modules": convert_to_regular_types(self.config.model.target_modules),
                    "exclude_modules": convert_to_regular_types(self.config.model.exclude_modules),
